prompt:
Task: HD remaster of a sheet of animation frames from the 1995 adventure game The Dig (LucasArts), in the smooth, detailed style approved for the main characters. This is a production asset. Every frame is fitted to the original frame's size and position afterwards, and the game lays it over the HD background with its own soft edges.

Input: the attached image is the original low-resolution sheet enlarged 4x with hard pixel edges. The frames stand apart on a plain flat cyan background (#00C8C8). Around the sheet is a plain gray (#808080) border. The border is only padding.

All frames on this sheet are animation frames of the same characters (Boston Low and Ludger Brink), as one scene, in different poses. On this sheet, row by row from left to right: animation 15, facing right (17 frames).

Do:
- Repaint every frame in high resolution with clean, natural detail: smooth shading instead of dithering, smooth anti-aliased outlines (no pixel steps), believable cloth, skin, hair and material.
- Keep the original look: the same character, the same colors, light direction, shadows and contrast, in the painted style of the approved HD sheets.
- Make all frames look identical apart from the pose: the same face, hair, clothes, colors and light in every frame. The frames are played one after another in the game, so any difference between them flickers.
- Keep the pose, proportions and silhouette of every frame as in the input, and keep each frame in its place on the sheet, in the same rows and the same order.
- Glowing effects (light, energy, lightning, sparks) are painted as soft glow that fades into transparency.

Do not:
- Do not add, remove, merge or redesign frames. Do not add anything between the frames: no shadows, floor, text, numbers, labels, frames or grid lines.
- Do not let frames touch or overlap each other.
- Some frames show only part of the character, for example a body without a head or a head alone, because the game draws the parts separately. Paint them as they are and do not complete them.
- Small bright magenta marks under the feet or at the edges are shadow markers used by the game. Leave them out; the game draws the shadow itself.
- No photorealism, no modern 3D look, no film grain, no vignette, no watermark, no signature.

Output: one PNG image, exactly 1536 x 1024 pixels, with a fully transparent background (real alpha, no background color and no gray border) and the frames in the same layout as the input. List the delivery with its sha256 in the fremdrift.json of your report and add a rutekart (the box around each frame's drawing) as for the main characters.

If a second image is attached, it is an already approved HD sheet of the same character, or an approved HD picture from the same game. Paint the character exactly as in that image: the same face, hair, clothes, colors and level of detail. Take all poses and the layout from the first image.


TOM-AUTHORIZED PRECISE SOURCE/STYLE CORRECTION:
Generate a native sheet from actual original source image1. Image2 is the source-checked same-variant17404 native candidate, with matching Boston and back-facing Brink drawing style, colors and original clothing. It is a continuity reference, not a different approval. Image5 is Tom-approved Brink face-only identity/drawn-style crop; use only short neat hair/drawn style, not its healthy skin palette or a front-facing pose. Image3 is a factual actual original-RGBA main-frame count/pose guide. Image4 is actual source palette evidence for Boston and BACK-FACING Brink. Their labels, swatches, backings and magenta markers are diagnostic only and must never appear in output. These roles override the generic description in the base prefix.
EXACT ACTUAL CONTENT: There are17 original COMPOSITE FRAMES arranged three rows[6,6,5]. EVERY FRAME contains BOTH distinct men, Boston on the left facing right and Brink on the right seen from behind, as ONE original composite scene sprite. Thus17 sourceframes and34 visible people. Do not turn pairs into separate frames, delete a person, duplicate one character, add a third person, or leave any solo figure. Preserve source relative scale, distance, occlusion/contact, shoulders, overlapping hands/artifact and feet in EVERY original frame. Keep each entire pair safely separate from its neighbors. Copy subtle original head/mouth/hand/jacket changes for all17 source phases in original row order, not identical clones.
BOSTON is brown-haired with pronounced gray temple, square angular jaw, plain very dark navy SHORT-SLEEVE T-SHIRT without jacket or badge, bare forearms and hands, dark brown-ochre trousers, blue-black boots. Image2 controls this smooth drawn identity/style. Boston holds a SMALL irregular white/gray CURVED artifact near Brink's shoulder/head at the original changing angle. Copy its exact source size/contour and bare finger/arm placement; not a large luminous ring, sphere, glove, weapon, shiny new sculpture or other invented prop. The object emits NO glow in this source.
BRINK is the blond man in a green-gray LONG-SLEEVE JACKET, dark brown trousers and dark boots, FROM BEHIND in every frame. Preserve the original back-of-head/hair, ear glimpse, jacket back seams, original raised forearm/palm and stance. Do not rotate him toward the viewer; no front eyes, mouth, face or chest badge on his back. No added badge, accessories or new clothing. Never turn Boston into blond Brink or Brink into a second Boston.
SOURCE COLORS/AMBIENT: subdued green/olive lighting ON the surfaces only. Boston skin lightRGB139,127,67, mid123,107,51, shadow91,71,27, muted OLIVE/YELLOW-TAN, not healthy peach/pink/red-orange. Very dark navy shirt23,35,43 /15,23,31. Dark trouser family115,63,0 /95,51,7 /75,35,0, not fresh vivid orange. Brink jacket95,135,115 /63,103,95 /39,71,75, green-lit blond hair151,175,47 /99,111,31; olive skin. Preserve material/ambient hue families and consistent shade across all frames, smooth natural drawn highlights allowed without flat exact-color filling. No neon green skin, resurrection damage, grain, plastic/3D or photographic look. Clean angular drawn contour/shadow planes, smooth antialiasing, same skull/head/neck/body scale across frames.
CLEAN TRANSPARENCY: source174 has NO external glow/bloom/halo. Green light belongs to body surfaces only. Alpha0 background and all spaces outside silhouettes. No diffuse brown/white/green matte field, artifact halo, floor, cast shadow, cloud, vignette or outline haze. Preserve immediate edge antialiasing, not broad background fade. Retain every real source limb/finger/prop, omit only magenta technical footmarks. Output1536x1024 RGBA, exact17 source pairs[6,6,5], no text, digits, labels, grid/boxes, unrelated heads/bodies or marks between frames.

SPECIFIC CORRECTIONS TO AVOID PREVIOUS NATIVE FAILURES: The source has clean smooth DRAWN contour and angular defined shadow planes, as image2 and image5, not realistic 3D airbrushed body volume, fabric rendering or textured hair. Brink has SHORT NEAT COMBED BLOND HAIR in smooth large drawn planes like image5, with original back-view silhouette as image1, olive-lit palette as image4. No curled fluffy hair, random pebbly grains, spongy curls, spikes or altered hairline. Boston clothing follows original seams and folds only: DO NOT invent projecting CARGO POUCHES, straps, newly outlined patch pockets, knee pads, chest marks or more outfit details than the source. His original trousers are ordinary dark brown trousers with source fold shadows. Preserve exact original garment silhouette. All17 Boston heads must reproduce their own original head tilt and speaking MOUTH/JAW state; open exactly where the original mouth is open, closed exactly where source is closed. Do not replace the animation with seventeen cloned closed-mouth poses. Skull, hair, eye position and neck scale stay stable; only actual mouth/jaw/tilt phases change. Small original finger/artifact changes remain. Exact17 original composite pairs[6,6,5], no external matte/glow or new objects.
